blockers.description: NEW BYTE-LOSS REGRESSION (green on base, red at tip, mutation-proven): InputCursorRegistry.pop_frame (psh/io_redirect/input_cursor.py:236-239) unconditionally destroys the cursor of whatever description the frame left on the fd — but when the frame's binding was created by bind_dup it is an ALIAS to a description ANOTHER fd still names. Popping a per-command dup frame therefore destroys the live cursor of fd 0 (or of the dup source) and every byte it was holding vanishes. This is exactly the defect class the slot exists to close (leg B, 'reaches no reader at all'), reintroduced through a different door, and it FALSIFIES the user-guide text this same branch adds ('a duplicated descriptor (exec 3<&0) shares them because it shares the source'). Fix must not drop a description still present in _fd_to_desc. The dev's 96-node suite is blind to it: the per-command dup cell has no third read, and every timeout cell runs inside a pipeline, where this route is not taken.

  R1/R2/N4/N5/N6 all go GREEN (b=<A>, L=<ABC>) while the slot's own leg-B row R3 stays GREEN.

INCOMPLETENESS OF THE CLAIMED CLOSE from the same defect — N9: exec 3<&0; read -N 1 a; true 4<&3; read -N 1 -u 3 b (stdin \xc3ABC\n): BASE psh b=<B>, TIP psh b=<B>, bash-C b=<A>. Dup aliasing does not survive an intervening frame, so leg B is only closed when nothing dups in between.

blockers.description: NEW BYTE-REORDERING REGRESSION, distinct root cause: IOManager.cursor_scope_fds (psh/io_redirect/manager.py:352-354) derives the frame's target fd as '0 if redirect.type.startswith("<") else 1' whenever redirect.fd is None. For a named-fd redirect ({v}<&n, {v}<file) redirect.fd IS None because the fd number is only allocated at apply time — so the frame scopes fd 0, which the redirect never re-points, and never scopes the fd it actually creates. Consequence: a read carrying a {v}<&0 redirect is hidden from its OWN description's buffered bytes, which then resurface in the following read — the bytes are reordered. Secondary consequence: the allocated fd's binding is left unscoped and dangles in _fd_to_desc after the frame pops.

  BASE psh: a=<\303> b=<A> c=<B>   bash-C: a=<\303> b=<A> c=<B>  -> AGREE
  TIP  psh: a=<\303> b=<B> c=<A>   bash-C: a=<\303> b=<A> c=<B>  -> DIVERGE (order swapped)

Distinct-cause proof: replayed against the tip copy carrying the BLOCKER-1 pop_frame mutation — P1 is STILL RED there (b=<B> c=<A>), so it is not a symptom of the pop_frame defect.

The dev's only named-fd cell, test_dup_spelling_shares_the_surplus[named-fd], uses the PERMANENT 'exec {v}<&0' spelling, which never enters a builtin frame, so it passes.

blockers.description: REGRESSION (green at base, byte-destroying at tip): the new alias bookkeeping made the registry's two cursor-drop sites reference-blind. InputCursorRegistry.pop_frame (input_cursor.py:227) and rebind (input_cursor.py:181) drop a description's cursor without checking whether ANOTHER fd still references that description. After bind_dup creates an alias, (a) any builtin carrying a per-command dup whose source fd holds buffered cursor state destroys that state at frame pop (manager.py:1075 restore path), and (b) `exec`-closing or rebinding the alias fd destroys the shared cursor via rebind (command.py:1085). Buffered bytes (malformed-split surplus or a held -t timeout partial) are then delivered to NO reader — precisely the 'no byte may reach no reader at all' property this slot's leg-B headline claims to close, and it falsifies the landed input_cursor.py docstring ('the held bytes can no longer reach another source or be lost') and the new user-guide sentence ('no input is lost either way'). Ordinary idioms trigger it: `true 3<&0` between two reads; `exec 3<&0; exec 3<&-` (the standard save/close-stdin pattern); `exec 4>&3; exec 4>&-`; output dups to a read fd (`>&0`). None of the 16 contract cells, 17 registry cells, or 5 M8 arms covers a pop/rebind of a still-referenced description (the dev's per-command dup cell consumes the surplus inside the frame, so pop always fires on an empty cursor).

Clean MATCH-at-base -> DIVERGE-at-tip regressions (C locale, stdin \xc3AB\n unless noted): X1 `read -N 1 a; true 3<&0; read -N 1 b; read -N 1 c` -> bash b=A c=B, tip b=B c=Z (byte A destroyed; base matched bash). X3 `read -N 1 a; true >&0; read -N 1 b` -> bash b=A, tip b=B (base matched). X4 `read -N 1 a; exec 3<&0; exec 3<&-; read -N 1 b` -> bash b=A, tip b=B (base matched). W6 `exec 3<h(\xc3KLM); read -N1 -u3 a; exec 4>&3; exec 4>&-; read -N1 -u3 b` -> bash b=K, tip b=L (base matched). Conservation regressions (timeout route, UTF-8, r1=142 validity control both shells): X5 strand \xc3 then `true 3<&0`, feed \xa9Z -> bash total \xc3\xa9Z, tip total \xa9Z (\xc3 destroyed; base conserved \xc3\xa9Z); X6 strand; exec 3<&0; true 3<&0 -> tip loses \xc3 (base conserved, reordered); X2 `read -N 2 -u 3 b 3<&0` leaving surplus on the shared cursor at pop -> bash c=B, tip c=\n (B destroyed). Deterministic on re-run. Registry-level mechanism demo at tip: bind_dup(9,r) after cursor exists on r, push_frame([9])+pop_frame -> cursor_for_fd(r) is no longer the outer cursor (False); bind_dup(9,r)+rebind(9) -> same destruction (False). All 16 contract cells + both M8 lock files green at this same tip, i.e. the defect escapes the shipped suite.

blockers.description: Dup-site census incomplete and the gap is UNDECLARED: compound-command per-command dups (`{ ...; } 3<&0`, `while ...; done 3<&0`) run through guarded_redirections -> apply_redirections, which got frame scoping (_scoped_input_cursors) but NO bind_dup call — dup_alias_fds is consulted only on the exec path (command.py), the builtin-frame path (manager.py DUP_FD branch), and the {v}<&n allocator (file_redirect.py). Inside such a frame the dup'd fd gets a FRESH frame-scoped cursor, so held/surplus bytes on the source fd are not visible through the dup — the same divergence class as the I1 (b) face this slot claims closed (bytes surface on the wrong read vs bash; conserved but reordered). This is pre-existing behavior (identical at base), so it is not a regression — but under the ruled CLOSE-both-surfaces outcome it is a divergent dup spelling left unfixed AND undeclared: the only registered open row is I1 (d), and the landed docs overclaim universal closure (io_redirect/CLAUDE.md: 'a DUP aliases the instance -> both fds share one cursor'; input_cursor.py docstring 'Dup — exec 3<&0 makes one description wear two fds ... both fds share one cursor'; user-guide: 'a duplicated descriptor (exec 3<&0) shares them because it shares the source'). Task check 3's rule — every dup spelling aliases the OpenDescription or carries a declared reason — fails for this spelling: no declared reason exists anywhere in the tree (grep for a compound-dup caveat comes back empty).
blockers.evidence: At tip 2f355fc3 vs live bash 5.2.26: X7 (UTF-8, strand \xc3 with r1=142 control, then `{ read -t 4 -u 3 y; } 3<&0`, feed \xa9Q) -> bash v=\xc3 y=\xa9Q w='', psh v='' y=\xa9Q w=\xc3 — fd 3 never saw the held byte; it surfaced on fd 0's LATER read (bytes conserved, wrong stream position). X8 (C locale, stdin \xc3ABZ\n, `read -N 1 a; { read -N 1 -u 3 b; } 3<&0; read -N 1 c`) -> bash b=A c=B, psh b=B c=A (swapped). Identical psh output at base e3924ed3 (replayed both ends). Code: guarded_redirections manager.py:392-420 applies _scoped_input_cursors + apply_redirections; FileRedirector.apply_redirections has no dup_alias_fds/bind_dup call for plain n<&m (only the {v} named path, file_redirect.py:651). The dev's own suite covers brace-group/while-loop frames for OPEN redirects only, never a compound dup.

issues.description: NEW BYTE-LOSS REGRESSION (green on base, red at tip, mutation-proven): InputCursorRegistry.pop_frame (psh/io_redirect/input_cursor.py:236-239) unconditionally destroys the cursor of whatever description the frame left on the fd — but when the frame's binding was created by bind_dup it is an ALIAS to a description ANOTHER fd still names. Popping a per-command dup frame therefore destroys the live cursor of fd 0 (or of the dup source) and every byte it was holding vanishes. This is exactly the defect class the slot exists to close (leg B, 'reaches no reader at all'), reintroduced through a different door, and it FALSIFIES the user-guide text this same branch adds ('a duplicated descriptor (exec 3<&0) shares them because it shares the source'). Fix must not drop a description still present in _fd_to_desc. The dev's 96-node suite is blind to it: the per-command dup cell has no third read, and every timeout cell runs inside a pipeline, where this route is not taken.

issues.description: NEW BYTE-REORDERING REGRESSION, distinct root cause: IOManager.cursor_scope_fds (psh/io_redirect/manager.py:352-354) derives the frame's target fd as '0 if redirect.type.startswith("<") else 1' whenever redirect.fd is None. For a named-fd redirect ({v}<&n, {v}<file) redirect.fd IS None because the fd number is only allocated at apply time — so the frame scopes fd 0, which the redirect never re-points, and never scopes the fd it actually creates. Consequence: a read carrying a {v}<&0 redirect is hidden from its OWN description's buffered bytes, which then resurface in the following read — the bytes are reordered. Secondary consequence: the allocated fd's binding is left unscoped and dangles in _fd_to_desc after the frame pops.

issues.description: REGRESSION (green at base, byte-destroying at tip): the new alias bookkeeping made the registry's two cursor-drop sites reference-blind. InputCursorRegistry.pop_frame (input_cursor.py:227) and rebind (input_cursor.py:181) drop a description's cursor without checking whether ANOTHER fd still references that description. After bind_dup creates an alias, (a) any builtin carrying a per-command dup whose source fd holds buffered cursor state destroys that state at frame pop (manager.py:1075 restore path), and (b) `exec`-closing or rebinding the alias fd destroys the shared cursor via rebind (command.py:1085). Buffered bytes (malformed-split surplus or a held -t timeout partial) are then delivered to NO reader — precisely the 'no byte may reach no reader at all' property this slot's leg-B headline claims to close, and it falsifies the landed input_cursor.py docstring ('the held bytes can no longer reach another source or be lost') and the new user-guide sentence ('no input is lost either way'). Ordinary idioms trigger it: `true 3<&0` between two reads; `exec 3<&0; exec 3<&-` (the standard save/close-stdin pattern); `exec 4>&3; exec 4>&-`; output dups to a read fd (`>&0`). None of the 16 contract cells, 17 registry cells, or 5 M8 arms covers a pop/rebind of a still-referenced description (the dev's per-command dup cell consumes the surplus inside the frame, so pop always fires on an empty cursor).
